title: Daynori Proxy Trust, Rate Limiter Ingress Hardening, and Spoofing Defense Verification

ingressArchitecture.edgeProxy: Cloudflare Edge Network (TLS termination, DDoS filtering, CDN caching, CF-Connecting-IP injection)
ingressArchitecture.originProxy: Render PaaS Internal Router / Load Balancer (Carrier-Grade NAT 100.64.0.0/10 and RFC 1918 10.0.0.0/8)
ingressArchitecture.applicationServer: Fastify 5 / Node.js 24 with CIDR-restricted trustProxy and ProcessLocalRateLimiter

empiricalIngressProofs.finding: Cloudflare Edge firewall actively intercepts and blocks external clients attempting to supply or inject CF-Connecting-IP.
empiricalIngressProofs.securityInvariant: CF-Connecting-IP is untampered when received via Cloudflare Edge; however, if origin is accessed directly bypassing Cloudflare, Render does not sanitize CF-Connecting-IP. Application must verify Cloudflare peer IP before trusting CF-Connecting-IP.

empiricalIngressProofs.finding: Proxies append remote client IP to the right side of X-Forwarded-For rather than overwriting it. Client-supplied values appear on the left.
empiricalIngressProofs.securityInvariant: Leftmost IP extraction (e.g. xff.split(',')[0]) is completely vulnerable to spoofing. The application MUST traverse X-Forwarded-For from right to left, stopping at the first untrusted proxy hop.

vulnerabilitiesRemediated.title: Unauthenticated Rate Limiter Header Spoofing Bypass
vulnerabilitiesRemediated.rootCause: ProcessLocalRateLimiter previously trusted any client-supplied CF-Connecting-IP or leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry. An attacker could bypass IP throttling by randomizing these headers.
vulnerabilitiesRemediated.remediation: Implemented resolveClientIp in apps/api/src/config/trustedProxies.ts using strict right-to-left traversal against verified Cloudflare and private/CGNAT CIDRs. Forged headers are discarded unless the direct socket peer or upstream chain contains verified Cloudflare IPs.
vulnerabilitiesRemediated.verification: tests/security/phase124-proxy-trust-and-rate-limiter.test.ts passed: untrusted clients randomizing headers remain strictly throttled.

vulnerabilitiesRemediated.title: Wildcard Proxy Trust in Fastify Server Configuration
vulnerabilitiesRemediated.rootCause: Fastify server was initialized with trustProxy: true, trusting all upstream proxies unconditionally.
vulnerabilitiesRemediated.remediation: Restricted trustProxy to TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS (official Cloudflare IPv4/IPv6 ranges, RFC 1918 private subnets, and RFC 6598 CGNAT subnets used by Render).
vulnerabilitiesRemediated.verification: Typecheck and integration tests confirm strict CIDR evaluation.

vulnerabilitiesRemediated.title: Brute-Force Attack Window on Sensitive Endpoints
vulnerabilitiesRemediated.rootCause: Standard 60 req/min rate limit applied uniformly across all endpoints, which was too permissive for authentication, password recovery, and account deletion.
vulnerabilitiesRemediated.remediation: Added sensitive route pattern detection enforcing a strict 10 req/min limit per resolved client IP on auth login, recovery, reset, registration, and account deletion endpoints.
vulnerabilitiesRemediated.verification: Unit tests confirm 10 req/min enforcement on /v1/auth/* and /v1/deletion/* with Retry-After header on 429.

multiInstanceBehaviorAndLimitations.storageMechanism: In-memory process-local Map (sliding window per Node.js process).
multiInstanceBehaviorAndLimitations.clusterMultiplier: In a horizontally scaled deployment with N instances behind a round-robin load balancer, effective cluster rate limit is up to N * limit per window.
multiInstanceBehaviorAndLimitations.mitigation: Tight sensitive route threshold (10 req/min) ensures that even across 2-3 instances, total attempts are capped at 20-30 req/min, preventing effective brute force.
multiInstanceBehaviorAndLimitations.futureRecommendation: For cluster sizes > 3 instances or > 1,000 MAU, deploy Redis-backed rate limiting (e.g. ioredis + lua token bucket) or configure Cloudflare Edge Rate Limiting Rules.
